list.text: AIRPLANE SIMULATOR: a first-person flight simulator built entirely out of Desmos math. Close this list (arrow at the top left) so the cockpit fills the screen, then press TAKEOFF or FLY IN THE AIR.

Controls: drag the amber throttle lever (bottom left) up for power. Drag the stick (bottom right square): sideways to bank and turn, down to pull the nose up and climb, up to push the nose down. FLAPS give extra lift at low speed (use them for take-off and landing). INVERT flips the stick up/down. CENTER STICK levels everything out. VIEW (top left) switches between the cockpit and a 3rd-person camera behind the plane. TIME (top right) switches between day and night.

Take-off: full throttle, wait until the speed reads about 60 knots, then pull the stick back. Landing: line up with the runway, about 70 knots, flaps down, throttle low, gently flare, and touch down with a sink rate under 800 ft/min, wings level, on the runway. Hills, water and a hard landing are all crashes!

list.label: THROTTLE UP, THEN PULL BACK AT 60 KT
Fly over hills, coast and sea.  Take off from runway 36 and land again.
THROTTLE: drag the amber lever (bottom left). Up = more power.
STICK: drag the dot inside the square (bottom right).
sideways = bank and turn      down = nose up (climb)      up = nose down
TAKEOFF: full throttle, hold the runway line, pull back at about 60 knots.
FLAPS: more lift at low speed. Use them to take off and to land.
LANDING: about 70 knots, flaps down, throttle low, line up with the runway,
ease the nose up just before touchdown. Sink under 800 ft/min, wings level.
Hills, water, a hard landing or leaving the runway at speed is a crash.
Land and come to a full stop on the runway to finish.
Hard landing: too fast, too steep or not level.
